```json
{"ranking": ["M8", "M7", "M4"], "fault": "PMOS cascode gate-bias diode M8 (pc generator) is mis-sized (too large W or too small L), or its bias current from M7 is reduced. This leaves pc too high, so the M3 pull-up is weak or off. The output is then pulled to ground (vout_dc ~0.03 V), the M1/M2 stack goes into triode, and gain and GBW collapse."}
```

This is a best estimate from DC reasoning alone. I did not run a simulation, so the ranking is not confirmed. The low vout_dc and the roughly -13.7 dB gain point to the output being pulled low by a weak pull-up, which implicates the pc bias chain first. The tail mirror M4 is third because a tail-current error would explain the low GBW, but it does not explain the output stuck near ground as well.
